::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Find the coefficient of $x^{-2}$ in the expansion of $(x-1)^3(\frac{1}{x} +2x)^6$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3653549/find-the-coefficient-of-x-2-in-the-expansion-of-x-13-frac1x-2x6), asked by [rash](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/650763/rash) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2020-05-01; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> >Find the coefficient of $x^{-2}$ in the expansion of $(x-1)^3(\frac{1}{x} +2x)^6$.
>
> I have tried finding out the general term of the whole expression.
>
> Then, I get the result as such 
> $$[(-1)^r {3 \choose r}(x^{3-r})][q-{6 \choose r} (2x)^{6-r}(\frac{1}{x})^r]$$
> But after solving for I get $r = 11/3$
>
> I think I am doing it wrong by just multiplying the general term. I don't know how else to continue. Please help.
>
> Thank You!
>
> Edit : *There was a typo in the question*
:::

You have two binomial powers, so you need two separate binomial expansions.
$$\begin{align*}
    (x-1)^3\left(\frac{1}{x} + 2x\right)^6
    &= \sum_{r=0}^3 \binom{3}{r}(-1)^r x^{3-r}
       \sum_{s=0}^6 \binom{6}{s}(2x)^{6-s}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)^s
  \\&= \sum_{r=0}^3\sum_{s=0}^6\binom{3}{r}\binom{6}{s}(-1)^r 2^{6-s} x^{(3-r)+(6-s)-s}
\end{align*}$$
If you want the coefficient of $x^{-2}$, you need to find the pairs $(r,s)$ with $0 \leq r \leq 3$ and $0 \leq s \leq 6$ such that
$$\begin{align*}
    (3-r)+(6-s) - s &= -2 \\
\iff
    9-r-2s &= -2 \\
\iff
    r+2s &= 11
\end{align*}$$
